TESTIMONY OF MICHAEL J. ALLEN, ASSOCIATE COMMISSIONER FOR TAX POLICY
DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE AND FINANCIAL SERVICES
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Taxation Hearing Date: April 23, 2025, Wednesday at 1:00 P.M.
LD 1505 - "An Act to Phase out the Sales and Use Tax"
Senator Grohoski, Representative Cloutier, and members of the Taxation Committee - good afternoon, my name is Michael Allen, Associate Commissioner for Tax Policy in the Department of Administrative and Financial Services. I am testifying at the request of the Administration Against LD 1505, "An Act to Phase out the Sales and Use Tax."
This bill would reduce each sales tax rate by 1/2 of a percentage point every 2 years, beginning January 1, 2026, until the rate is 0% for each category of tangible personal property or taxable service subject to sales tax. If enacted, the rate of 5.5% would be finally reduced to 0% in 2046, and the rate of 10% would reach 0% in 2064. The bill would also biennially require the assessor to submit to the Taxation Committee a bill codifying reduced rates--it should be amended to instead require that the bill be submitted by the Department of Administrative and Financial Services.
If the bill is enacted, MRS would be required to update the Sales and Use Tax Return every two years. Administrative costs are under review but would be potentially substantial. With respect to fiscal impact, the sales and use tax currently raises $2.4 billion on an annual basis.
1

The Administration looks forward to working with the Committee on the bill; representatives from MRS will be here for the Work Session to provide additional information and respond in detail to the Committee's questions.

Testimony In Support of

LD 1505 An Act t0 Phase out the Sales and Use Tax

Good Afternoon Senator Grohoski, Rep. Cloutier and my esteemed colleagues and
Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Taxation, I am State Representative Shelley Rudnicki representing District 67, the towns of Fairfield and Benton. I am here
to bring forward LD 1505 An Act to Phase out the Sales and Use Tax

In 1951 when sales tax was brought into Maine, the sales tax was 2% with 22 exemptions. Presently, the sales tax is 5.5% with over 100 different exemptions which we keep adding to.

On Oct 1 2013 - June 30, 2015 sales tax was increased from 5% to 5.5%. It was supposed to be
temporary. We all know what temporary in the legislature means.

This bill is simple and will take the sales tax down to zero. Every 2 years the sales tax will be reduced by .5%. It will take 12 years to get to zero which will ease the impact on state revenues.

This bill will go right to the heart of helping low income and fixed income Mainers.
